judged_text: The sync-mode fetch has no timeout, status check, or error handling, and the endpoint URL/env-var gating is duplicated as the same two-condition check in both refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse. When the sync endpoint is slow or down, every calendar operation hangs on an unbounded fetch (calendar reads are on the booking hot path); and the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` pair is hand-maintained in multiple files, so the next sync-aware call site can easily enable only one half of the mode.

When the sync endpoint is slow or down, every calendar operation hangs on an unbounded fetch (calendar reads are on the booking hot path); and the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` pair is hand-maintained in multiple files, so the next sync-aware call site can easily enable only one half of the mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no timeout/abort signal and no `response.ok`/status handling before returning the Response. Separately, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` re-implements the same gating (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) to choose a different schema, duplicating the mode conditions across files. These are concrete robustness/maintainability issues introduced by the change (potentially causing long waits if the endpoint is slow/down and making it easy for future call sites to update only one side of the gating).
